title: lupinus sierrae-blancae subsp. aquilinus
intro: Lupinus sierrae-blancae subsp. aquilinus, commonly known as the Sierra Blanca lupine or the Sierra Blanca lupine subsp. aquilinus, is a rare and endemic plant species found in the Sierra Blanca Mountains of New Mexico, USA. It is a perennial herb belonging to the legume family and is known for its vibrant purple flowers. The plant has been reported to have various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities, which may be attributed to its ability to stimulate the immune system and reduce oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of Lupinus sierrae-blancae subsp. aquilinus include alkaloids, flavonoids, and saponins, which are believed to possess therapeutic actions such as anti-hypertensive, anti-diabetic, and anti-cancer properties.
